$doc: Vyomi capability registry — GCP Firestore. See aws/s3.json for the contract. Feature ids share one namespace with the AWS registry, so they are prefixed gcp.firestore.*

gcp.firestore.databases.title: Databases (list, create, get, update, delete)
limitations: Database create/update/delete complete synchronously in Vyomi; the real API returns a long-running operation to poll.

gcp.firestore.documents.title: Collections and documents (create, get, list, merge, delete) and the Firestore Studio data viewer

gcp.firestore.query-builder.title: Query builder (structured queries: field filters, composite AND/OR, orderBy, limit)

gcp.firestore.indexes.title: Composite indexes (create, list, delete)
limitations: Indexes report state READY immediately; Vyomi does not model the real console's transient BUILDING phase, and it does not reject queries that would need a missing index.

gcp.firestore.single-field-exemptions.title: Single-field index exemptions
limitations: Per-field index-exemption overrides round-trip through the fields API, but Vyomi always indexes every field automatically regardless of an exemption — the override is stored, not enforced.

gcp.firestore.vector-indexes.title: Vector indexes (for vector-similarity search)
limitations: Vyomi has no vector field type or similarity search engine, so vector indexes cannot be created or used.

gcp.firestore.ttl.title: Time-to-live (TTL) policies
limitations: Setting a field's ttlConfig is real and round-trips, but Vyomi never runs the background sweep that deletes expired documents — documents past their TTL timestamp are not actually removed.

gcp.firestore.security-rules.title: Security rules editor
limitations: Vyomi stores and returns the rules source exactly as written through its own getSecurityRules/updateSecurityRules endpoints (real Firestore security rules are managed by the separate Firebase Rules API), but it never evaluates the rules against a request — every document read/write Vyomi allows is unconditional.

gcp.firestore.import-export.title: Import / Export (exportDocuments / importDocuments)
limitations: Export/import calls are accepted and recorded as completed operations on the Import/Export page exactly like the real console, but Vyomi does not actually read or write Cloud Storage objects — no real file transfer happens.

gcp.firestore.backups.title: Backup schedules and backups
limitations: Creating a backup schedule is real and immediately takes one backup (there is no background scheduler in Vyomi to fire later ticks on the daily/weekly recurrence), and a backup cannot be restored into a new database.

gcp.firestore.point-in-time-recovery.title: Point-in-time recovery (PITR)
limitations: The pointInTimeRecoveryEnablement setting round-trips on the database resource, but Vyomi keeps no change history to recover from — enabling it does not let you actually restore an earlier version of a document.

gcp.firestore.insights.title: Insights (query and index usage recommendations)
limitations: Vyomi collects no query-performance telemetry, so it has nothing to generate index or query insights from.

gcp.firestore.usage.title: Usage dashboard (reads/writes/deletes/storage charts)
limitations: Vyomi does not meter per-operation usage over time, so it cannot render the usage charts the real console builds from Cloud Monitoring metrics.

gcp.firestore.key-visualizer.title: Key Visualizer
limitations: Key Visualizer renders a heatmap of real production key-access load; Vyomi records no per-key traffic histograms to visualize.
